title: Aspect and time
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Pretérito perfeito composto: tenho + participle for repeated action up to now
lessons.explanation: In Portuguese the perfeito composto (tenho + participle) does not mean a single finished event, as the English present perfect often does. It means an action that has repeated, or a situation that has kept going, up to now: Tenho trabalhado muito ultimamente (I have been working a lot lately). For one completed event, use the simple perfeito: Já comi (I have eaten). Form it with the present of ter plus the unchanging participle: tenho feito, tens feito, tem feito, temos feito, têm feito. It often appears with ultimamente, nos últimos meses and desde que.

examples.en: Lately I have been sleeping little.

examples.pt: Ela tem viajado muito este ano.
examples.en: She has been travelling a lot this year.

examples.pt: Nós temos estudado português todas as noites.
examples.en: We have been studying Portuguese every night.

lessons.title: Estar + gerúndio: actions in progress, now and then
lessons.explanation: Use estar + gerúndio for an action in progress at the moment you speak or at a past moment. Brazilian Portuguese uses the gerúndio, not the European a + infinitive. Form the gerúndio by replacing the infinitive ending: -ar becomes -ando (falando), -er becomes -endo (comendo), -ir becomes -indo (partindo). Irregular: pôr gives pondo, vir gives vindo, ter gives tendo. Present: Estou lendo. Past in progress: Estava lendo quando você ligou. The gerúndio does not change for person or gender, and estar changes as usual.

lessons.title: Aspect verbs: acabar de, começar a, voltar a, deixar de, continuar a
lessons.explanation: These verbs plus an infinitive show a stage of an action. Acabar de + infinitive means to have just done something: Acabei de chegar (I just arrived). Começar a + infinitive is to start doing: Começou a chover. Voltar a + infinitive is to do again: Voltei a estudar. Deixar de + infinitive is to stop doing: Deixei de fumar. Continuar a (or continuar + gerúndio, common in Brazil) is to keep doing: Continuo a trabalhar, or Continuo trabalhando. Mind the preposition: acabar de, começar a, voltar a, deixar de, continuar a.

lessons.title: Já, ainda and ainda não with present, perfeito and future
lessons.explanation: Já means already or by now: Já comi (I have already eaten). Ainda means still: Ainda moro aqui. Ainda não means not yet: Ainda não comi. With the perfeito, já shows the action is done, and ainda não shows it has not happened up to now. In questions, Já comeu? asks whether it is done. With the present, ainda means a situation continues: Ele ainda está dormindo. With the future, já means very soon: Já volto (I will be right back). Word order is flexible, but ainda não stays together and goes before the verb.

examples.en: I have already had lunch, thanks.

examples.en: My brother still lives with my parents.

lessons.title: Duration and time since: há, faz, desde, durante, atrás
lessons.explanation: Há and faz both mean ago or for when they count time. Há dois anos que moro aqui and Faz dois anos que moro aqui mean I have lived here for two years. With a past event, há or atrás gives time ago: Cheguei há dois dias, or Cheguei dois dias atrás. Do not use há and atrás together. Desde marks the starting point: Moro aqui desde 2020. Durante marks the span: Estudei durante três horas. Brazilians often use faz in speech and há in writing. Desde does not take a time length, and durante does not take a starting point.

examples.en: I have lived here for three years.
I have worked at this company since 2019.
